title: Space Force awards K2 Space $22.9 million for laser communications demonstration
summary: The U.S. Space Force has awarded K2 Space a $22.9 million contract to demonstrate laser communications using two satellites equipped with optical terminals. The goal is to enhance connectivity between military systems in orbit.

summary: China launched a Long March 6A rocket carrying a secretive TJS-27 satellite pair and a next-generation Tianlian relay satellite into a new orbit. The mission enhances China's on-orbit communications relay capabilities.

title: Sending repurposed Mars rover to the moon could cost more than $1 billion
summary: Repurposing a Mars rover for a lunar mission could cost NASA over $1 billion, a claim disputed by the agency's administrator.

title: Spain commits up to $2.3 billion for national military communications for IRIS²
summary: Spain will allocate between €1.6 billion and €2 billion ($1.8 to $2.3 billion) to develop a national military satellite communications constellation as part of the IRIS² program. The initiative aims to enhance secure military communications through a dedicated satellite network.

title: Inside the effort to show Congress what war in space looks like
summary: The Space Force Association’s National Spacepower Center is creating an unclassified environment to demonstrate satellite threats and their impacts on Earth for Congress. This effort aims to visualize potential space warfare scenarios and their consequences.

title: Space Force picks 15 companies for $981 million training range contract
summary: The U.S. Space Force has selected 15 companies to compete for a $981 million contract to develop satellites, sensors, and systems for military space training exercises. The vendors will build infrastructure to enable more realistic space warfare simulations.

title: NASA still assessing Starliner-1 flight opportunities
summary: NASA is making progress with Boeing's CST-100 Starliner but has not yet set a date for its next flight. The agency is still evaluating flight opportunities for the Starliner-1 mission.

summary: The article discusses the evolving dynamics of space warfare, drawing lessons from conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East. It highlights the growing militarization of space and its implications for global security.

summary: Experts emphasize the need for establishing rules of the road as companies develop large constellations of orbital data center satellites. The focus is on addressing critical space safety topics.

summary: NASA ended production of the Saturn V moon rocket on Aug. 1, 1968, due to budget concerns, marking a significant shift in the Apollo program just a year before the Apollo 11 moon landing.
